input: The performance of a centrifugal pump moving water between two vessels at grade was characterised at its duty point, and the picture that emerges is as follows. At the duty point in question, the flow delivered by the pump is 47 m3 h-1 against a head of 18 m, and the pump efficiency at this operating point is 69%. The shaft power required at the duty point works out at 3.3 kW. The motor that drives the pump is rated 15% above this value, which builds a measure of headroom into the installation over and above the power that the duty itself demands. As far as cavitation is concerned, it is reassuring to note that cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test; that test, however, ran for 4 h at the duty point only, so the observation is tied to that particular set of conditions and to that duration, and it would be imprudent to read it as a guarantee covering the whole of the pump's operating range or extended periods of running. More broadly, a duty point of this kind is the anchor for the whole installation, because the motor selection, the acceptance test, and the day-to-day operation of the pump all refer back to the same specified condition.
target: A centrifugal pump moves water between two vessels at grade. The two vessels at grade stand at the same elevation, so the head is developed against the system resistance rather than against a lift between levels. At the duty point the flow is 47 m3 h-1 against a head of 18 m, with pump efficiency of 69%. Shaft power at the duty point is 3.3 kW. The motor is rated 15% above this value, so the motor carries a stated margin over the shaft power at the duty point and no more than that margin can be inferred. Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test, which ran for 4 h at the duty point only. The duty point is the operating point at which the pump was tested and rated: the flow, head, efficiency, and shaft power all belong to that single point. Away from the duty point the pump follows its own characteristic, and none of the stated values describes operation at another flow. The cavitation statement is a detection statement with the same boundary: no cavitation was detected during a test of the stated duration at the stated point, and the test says nothing about longer runs or other operating points. At its tested scope, the result is a rated duty point with its shaft power and motor margin, and a cavitation observation bounded by the acceptance test.
